postTitle: Owning a Home With More Than Two People
topic: The title says who owns, the loan says who owes, and an agreement says what the group meant

assumptions.notes: No euro figures. From the post: lenders often cap the borrowers on one loan at somewhere between two and four, depending on lender and country; everyone named is liable for the whole debt; a departure usually means a new loan in fewer names. Four combinations of being on the title and on the loan. Rules vary by lender and country.

beats.narration: A home shared by a group runs on three separate documents. The title, the loan, and an agreement between the owners.
The title says who owns the home, and in what shares.
The loan says who owes. Lenders often cap it at two to four names, and every borrower owes the whole debt, not a share.
beats.subtext: Every borrower owes the whole debt

beats.narration: Only the agreement records what the group meant. What each person put in. How a share is bought out. What happens if someone stops paying.
A departure often needs a buyout and a new loan on fewer incomes. If that fails, the home may need to be sold.

caption.instagram:
Three names on a shared mortgage. Each of them owes all of it, not a third.

A home shared by a group runs on three documents. The title says who owns. The loan says who owes: lenders often cap it at two to four names, and every borrower owes the whole debt. Only an agreement between the owners records what each person put in, how a share is bought out, and what happens if someone stops paying. When one owner leaves, the others usually pay out the share and need a new loan on fewer incomes. If they cannot, the house may have to be sold.

Four positions on a title and a loan: on both, the title only, the loan only, or neither. On the loan only, a person owes the debt and owns nothing.
